statements: Requirements for implementing an ideal world model: 1. Encode all information to the boundary. 2. Conform to conformal symmetry. Follow this rule, flattens the world into a two-dimensional space, and visual generation is almost lossless world generation.

Definition of an ideal world model: 1. Spatial sequence 2. Time sequence 3. Dense representation 4. Semantic instances 5. World core 6. Physical constraint 7. RIVE, Reasonable, Interpretable, Visualizable, and Editable. 8. Bidirectional training and inference 9. All living animals have posture information.
The method to make vision models understand physics is to create a core space and implement constraints within it.

Ideal world models possess conformal symmetry, e.g., representing data positions as relative positions, allowing the core space to have tremendous freedom and robustness. E.g., this can solve the fixed resolution problem in ViT and aligns with human intuition.

Adding high-dimensional features/the complexity of the latent space manifold itself (using WSG), and reducing the actual distribution of the latent space (based on flow models or physically consistent data) all contribute to semantic consistency.
The key to the World Snapshot Model is using WSG to record unified spatial information, creating multi-perspective consistency, human ID consistency, and behavior consistency.

The coordinates of a moving camera are one of the key pieces of information that help the model understand the world. Observing the world while moving is like querying a high-dimensional manifold, similar to how Earth is a sphere rather than a flat plane. Conventional generative models are equivalent to generating from a fixed perspective.

The principle of least action is the underlying principle of the world and can explain all known physical systems. Therefore, as long as we conform to the principle of least action, we hold the key to making models understand physics.
Composing and extending visual task paths can represent sudden changes such as a cup shattering or cars colliding. This is the final mile that visual models need to complete.

TunnelingNet is the training architecture of the World Snapshot Model. It learns compact task paths while preserving a shared generative backbone, allowing thousands of visual tasks to coexist in one model.
In the field of world snapshots, unified representations connect reconstruction, time-space, order, and existence with generation, rendering, understanding, and cognition.

In Computer Vision before WSM was proposed, all estimation tasks can be regarded as deriving WSG from images, all conditional generation tasks can be seen as generating WSG with fixed partial results, and all reconstruction tasks can be considered as obtaining WSG sets through known images.

The latent space of WSM has the characteristics of being Reasonable, Interpretable, Visualizable, and Editable. Unlike all previous works, the parameter latent space of previous models only has the simplest I/O interface.
